mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a highly accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% compared to periods where it is above (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where RSAFS increases by more than 2% MoM compared to periods where it does not (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% over 3 months compared to periods where it does not (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM compared to periods where it does not (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% over the same period, it signals a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% MoM
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where both HOUST increases by more than 5% MoM and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% MoM compared to periods where these conditions are not met (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods where CPIAUCSL increases by more than 2% YoY compared to periods where it does not (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 compared to periods where it does not (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5% over the same period, it signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% QoQ
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods where both GDPC1 increases by more than 2% QoQ and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% QoQ compared to periods where these conditions are not met (t-test p > 0.05).
